title: Pro trading appropriateness assessment
intro: SIMULATED placeholder questions pending Compliance review (OQ-C1). This short check makes sure you understand the risks of leveraged, fast-moving trading before the Pro terminal is unlocked. Your answers are graded on our server and not stored; only your score and the questionnaire version are kept.

questions.prompt: You open a position worth 30,000 with 1,000 of margin (1:30). The price moves 2% against you. Roughly what happens to your margin?

options.label: I lose about 2% of my 1,000 margin (about 20).
I lose about 600, which is 60% of my margin.
Nothing, because losses only count when I close.

questions.prompt: Your stop loss is at 100. The market closes at 101 and opens the next day at 95. At what price is your stop most likely to fill?

options.label: Exactly 100, a stop always fills at its price.
Around 95, the next available price, so the loss is bigger than planned.
It does not fill until the price returns to 100.

questions.prompt: Which costs reduce the result of a leveraged trade held for several days?

options.label: Only the commission when I open.
The spread, commissions and overnight funding (swap) for every night the position is open.
None, paper and leveraged trading have no costs.

questions.prompt: Your losses grow and your equity falls below the margin your positions need. What can happen?

options.label: Positions can be closed automatically at a loss.
The broker must wait until the market recovers.
Losses are capped at the margin I deposited in every case.

questions.prompt: You plan to risk at most 1% of a 10,000 account on a trade with a stop 50 points away. Each point is worth 1 per unit. What is the largest size?

options.label: 2 units (2 × 50 = 100, which is 1% of 10,000).
20 units.
As many units as my margin allows.

questions.prompt: A major economic announcement is due in five minutes. What is most likely around the release?

options.label: Spreads stay the same and prices move slowly.
Spreads can widen and prices can jump, so orders may fill far from what I expect.
The market closes during announcements.

questions.prompt: A trading robot's backtest shows a smooth, rising equity curve. What should you assume?

options.label: The robot will keep producing the same returns live.
Past and simulated results do not guarantee future results; live trading can lose money.
A robot cannot lose more than the backtest's worst day.

questions.prompt: Which money is appropriate to trade with leverage?

options.label: Money I can afford to lose without affecting my essential expenses.
My emergency savings, because returns are quick.
Borrowed money, to increase my position size.
